$comment: NORMATIVE BRAND SPECIFICATION FOR THE CONDUIT MARK.
This file is the single source of truth for Conduit's identity geometry.
Every other representation - the PNG/ICO/ICNS rasters, logo.svg,
ConduitLogo.tsx and conduit_logo.dart - is GENERATED from this file by
scripts/icons/build_icons.py. Never hand-edit a generated file; edit the
numbers here and run `npm run icons` (from apps/desktop).
The verifier (scripts/icons/verify_icons.py) fails if any generated file
differs from a fresh regeneration, so the assets cannot silently drift apart
the way four independent definitions previously did.
name: conduit-mark

rationale.summary: One unbroken channel of constant thickness, bending from a horizontal run into a diagonal descent and back out to a horizontal run. The two terminals are flat-cut sections, perpendicular to the tube axis, so the mark reads as a sectioned conduit rather than a letterform.
why: It is a real pipe offset. 'Conduit' is the product's name and the mark is a length of conduit, so the name is rendered rather than decorated.
One channel, exactly two terminals. There is no third exit, which is the product's architectural claim: LAN peer to phone, no cloud account, no telemetry.
The channel bends to reach across two devices and still arrives unbroken - continuity is the product's headline feature.
Constant thickness and flat-cut terminals read as engineering, not as the letter Z: no typeface sets Z with perpendicular end cuts and a constant-width spine.
Inherently asymmetric, so it cannot collapse into a cross, a plus, or a centred collar.
deliberately_not: chain link or any interlocking-link glyph (this was the previous mark; also reads as KDE Connect / LocalSend / Join)
cloud, globe or WiFi arcs (a cloud would be a false statement about the architecture)
lock, padlock, key or shield (docs/decisions/0007 and docs/SECURITY.md 4.9 state the encryption is NOT end-to-end; a padlock would be a claim the security docs forbid)
chat or speech bubble (SMS is one of nine features; a bubble would brand this as a messenger)
two device outlines or a network graph (reads as generic 'any app' or as enterprise MDM)
any gradient, glow filter, or stroke thinner than the tube width inside the mark

palette.$comment: Hex, sRGB. `ink` is the on-light-surface counterpart required by the design system; raw accent must never land on a light surface.

mark.$comment: Centreline of the tube, in 64-grid units, top-left origin, y down. The conduit is the union of one rotated rectangle per segment plus a disc at each interior joint. Terminals are NOT capped with a disc - they are flat sections, cut perpendicular to the axis.

rendering.$comment: The rasteriser is Pillow, pinned, and renders at SS x the target size then box-filters down. Supersampling is what gives the icons real antialiasing; the previous generator drew straight to the final size and produced alpha levels of only {0, 255}.

$comment: A variant is DATA, not a fork. Same geometry, same mark colour, same rasteriser
for all of them; only the plate treatment differs, and only because the
hosting OS mandates it:
- Apple rejects alpha in AppIcon PNGs and applies its own squircle mask,
- Android launchers apply their own mask to the legacy mipmap PNGs,
- Windows and Linux do not mask a window icon, so the desktop ships a
rounded plate that keeps transparent corners,
- macOS NSStatusItem template images use ONLY the alpha channel, so the
tray variant has no plate at all and is monochrome.
This is the one and only legitimate source of difference between platforms,
and it affects corner pixels only - never the mark, never the interior.

plate.description: Rounded plate, transparent corners. Desktop bundle icons, favicon.

plate-square.description: Full-bleed opaque plate. iOS AppIcon and Android mipmap, both of which are masked by the OS.

tray.description: Monochrome mark on transparency, no plate. macOS template image. Sits in the 22pt menu-bar slot, so the mark is inset to ~78% and uses a flatter optical weight.

mark.description: The bare mark on transparency, no plate. In-app React component, Flutter widget, tray fallback.

targets.$comment: Every platform asset in the repository, declared once. `npm run icons` renders every entry; `npm run icons:verify` proves every committed file matches and that nothing guarded is missing.

emittedSources.$comment: Code files generated from the same geometry. These are in-app UI, so they stay vector; every raster above is pre-rendered so the OS never re-rasterises on a machine we do not control.

excluded.$comment: Build output. Vite copies public/ verbatim into dist/; the copy is never committed and never hashed.
